- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp downward trend, adjust downward bias by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is overly optimistic, reduce forecast by 5–15% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check sentiment history for recent negative signals — if present, apply mean reversion correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5–7 days show consistent underperformance, shift the early forecast upward by 2–5% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or bearish), avoid over-optimistic forecasts — cap upward revisions at 3% unless sentiment spikes.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), use a 3–5 day smoothing filter on forecast to reduce noise and avoid erratic corrections.
